title: Jesse Price's battle with Buddy Rich
summary: Jesse Price boasted and was beaten by Rich with brushes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: We used to have a lot of battles there in Kansas City. Jesse Price, he was one of the main drummers.
In Kansas City at the time.

And I told him about Buddy Rich, and he said, 'Oh, he can't play no drums.' Said, 'I'll take my wire brushes and tear him up,' like that. I said, 'Now, just a minute, Jesse, now. You cannot play wire brushes like this guy plays wire brushes.'
He said, 'I'll show you, I'm going to meet him downtown tomorrow, and we're going to have a battle down there.'
And so they had met down there.

No, it was a little club right next to the College Inn, see. And so musicians came down with their horns, and so Jesse Price brought his snare drum and sock cymbal, saxophone, see. No bass drum. So -- he figured that Buddy couldn't play without a bass drum, one of those things.
But Buddy came there and just tore him up. And he
-- and Jesse Price said, 'You know, he can play drums, can't he?' I said, I told you, he just whupped you all over the place.
